content.text: No customer-payable liquidated damages, penalties, or early-termination charges exist anywhere in the agreement.

input.quote: 14. TERMINATION. Subject to Section 4 hereof, TrueLink will continue to provide the requested Hosting Services and Support Services until the last day of the month following the month in which Client provides TrueLink with a written notice of its election to terminate this Agreement.
input.rationale: The Agreement contains no liquidated damages, penalty, or stipulated-sum provision payable by Client. Searches for "liquidated damages", "penalty", "damages", "shall pay", "minimum", "late" and "interest" return nothing of that character. Compensation (§5) is limited to fees for services actually requested plus stated monthly minimums during the term, with a documentation/dispute right in Client's favour, and §6 caps Hosting Services price increases for the first year and benchmarks rates to TrueLink's best customer pricing. The termination provision (§14) imposes no exit fee: Client simply gives written notice and services (and therefore fees) run to the last day of the following month — an ordinary wind-down of roughly one month's fees, comfortably inside the fallback's 3-month cap even if characterised as an exit cost. The spam covenant in §7 and §8f is a conduct restriction enforced through TrueLink's technical and equitable remedies, not a per-incident stipulated penalty. This meets the preferred position (no liquidated damages or penalties payable by Customer), so no redline is warranted.
